discovery: Circuit quantum electrodynamics: strong coupling of superconducting artificial atoms to microwave photons
motivation: In 2004 Blais, Girvin and Schoelkopf proposed and then demonstrated that a superconducting qubit coupled to an on-chip microwave resonator reaches the strong-coupling regime of cavity QED, previously accessible only with real atoms. Circuit QED gave physics a new laboratory: vacuum Rabi splitting, photon-number-resolved spectroscopy, Fock and cat states of light, and quantum-nondemolition dispersive readout, all with engineered, wired artificial atoms. It also supplied the architecture of modern quantum processors: resonator-mediated coupling and readout, the transmon, and bosonic error-correcting codes that surpassed break-even. Today virtually every superconducting quantum computing effort worldwide, academic and industrial, is built on this framework. It is a rare case where a clean fundamental advance in light-matter interaction became, within two decades, the foundation of a new technology.
